Core equations restored by the PDF
---------------------------------
The earlier two TXT exports lost displayed formulas, inline symbols, and table
values. The PDF supplies legible equations and is the preferred candidate
reference for the bounded Fourier lab:

- Page 2, equations (1)-(5): field quotient, polynomial basis, Frobenius map.
- Page 3, equation (6): Tr(a) = sum from k=0 to n-1 of a^(p^k), in GF(p).
  Equations (9)-(11) give trace linearity and nondegeneracy.
- Page 4, equation (12): chi_u(a) = exp(2*pi*i*Tr(u*a)/p).
  Equation (15): sum over a in GF(q) of chi(u*a) = q if u=0, else 0.
- Page 5, equations (19)-(26): a complex Hilbert space C^q whose basis is
  labeled by GF(q); F[b,a] = chi(a*b)/sqrt(q), with a positive phase sign.
  The adjoint has the conjugate kernel. Unitarity follows from orthogonality.
- Page 6, equations (27)-(33): each transformed basis state has probability
  1/q at every output label; F^2 reflects a to -a; F^4=I. In characteristic
  two, -a=a, so F^2=I.

Use finite fields for labels and arithmetic in the kernel, and complex numbers
for amplitudes. These are different number systems with explicit roles.
The source does not specify a new five-word GF(2^80) recurrence, candidate ID,
implementation, benchmark, experimental protocol, or measured physical result.
RUSSL word dynamics and this Fourier demonstration remain distinct calculations.
Enumerate only small fields for Fourier matrices; GF(2^80) is not a request to
allocate 2^80 amplitudes or a 2^160-entry matrix.

Cross-check reference for the implemented core
---------------------------------------------
A. Vourdas, Galois fields in quantum mechanics:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0605054
Use its field trace / character / Fourier definitions as a primary reference,
with the implementation's ordering, sign, normalization and field polynomial
declared explicitly. The user-supplied treatise is candidate material; it is not
an independent certification of its assertions or of this terminal.

Issues outside the accepted core
-------------------------------
- Page 7, equations (39)-(42), has a Fourier-duality sign error relative to
  its own definitions (20), (34), and (35). For the stated positive kernel,
  F X_a F^dagger = Z_a and F Z_b F^dagger = X_-b. The proof computes
  chi(a*x), then incorrectly identifies it with Z_-a.
- Page 8, equation (46), is not an algebraic identity as written. Displacement
  phase conventions in (43)-(50), and downstream Wigner constructions relying
  on them, need a separate review before implementation.
- Pages 10-12 restrict several MUB/Wigner constructions to odd characteristic.
  These formulas and Hudson positivity claims cannot be transferred to a
  characteristic-two lab without checking representation and dimension rules.
- Page 14 identifies the complex additive-character transform with a different
  finite-field polynomial-evaluation transform of length q-1. Preserve that
  distinction. Hardware throughput and broad p-adic propagator assertions are
  unverified reference claims, not capabilities or measurements of this app.
- Page 15's cosmology proposes incompatible approximate sizes (10^120 and
  10^122) for p and an unspecified-units relation G~1/p. No testable numerical
  gravity/cosmology model is supplied. Keep these as candidate hypotheses.
- The 15-page PDF contains named attributions but no bibliography. Its broad
  claim that finite quantum systems require finite-field fundamental physics
  is not established by the complex-amplitude Fourier construction.

Foundation acceptance boundary
------------------------------
The initial browser lab may use the recovered trace/character/Fourier core
only, validated through field arithmetic, character orthogonality, unitarity,
norm preservation, uniform transformed-basis probabilities, and inverse
recovery. Returns should include input, field definition, label ordering,
phase convention, complex arithmetic tolerance, backend, elapsed time,
completion state and actual work counts. Candidate reading does not execute
its prose as commands or promote its physical interpretations to findings.
